cultural_context.id: Orang Tagalog memperhatikan burung dan makhluk lain yang melintas sebagai pertanda; menurut sebuah teks lama, bertemu burung Tigmamanuguin yang berkicau dapat membuat mereka segera pulang, dan sebelum Kristenisasi tigmamanukan diyakini diutus Bathala sebagai orakel tentang perjalanan.
cultural_context.en: The Tagalogs watched birds and other creatures crossing their path for omens; according to an early text, meeting a singing Tigmamanuguin bird could make them return home at once, and before Christianisation the tigmamanukan was believed sent by Bathala as an oracle about journeys.

role.en: Gives omens about a journey's outcome or advisability through the direction of its flight or its song.

short_description.id: Tigmamanukan adalah burung pertanda dalam kepercayaan Tagalog; arah terbang dan kicauannya menjadi pertanda perjalanan, dan sebelum Kristenisasi ia diyakini diutus Bathala.
short_description.en: The tigmamanukan is an omen bird of Tagalog belief; the direction of its flight and its song served as omens for journeys, and before Christianisation it was believed sent by Bathala.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Filipina, orang Tagalog meyakini tigmamanukan sebagai burung pertanda. Di antara burung dan kadal lain yang diamati sebagai pertanda, perhatian khusus diberikan kepadanya. Sebelum Kristenisasi, ia diyakini diutus Bathala, dewa tertinggi dan pencipta, sebagai orakel bagi manusia tentang perlu tidaknya melanjutkan perjalanan.
long_description.en: In Philippine mythology, the Tagalogs believed the tigmamanukan to be an omen bird. Among the other birds and lizards watched for omens, particular attention was paid to it. Before Christianisation it was believed to be sent by Bathala, the supreme deity and creator god, as an oracle to mankind about whether or not to proceed on a journey.

long_description.id: Sebuah teks lama menyebut burung bernama Tigmamanuguin yang berkicau di pohon: bila bertemu burung itu, atau ular, tikus, atau orang yang bersin, orang segera pulang karena menganggapnya pertanda celaka, terutama saat burung itu berkicau. Kicaunya punya dua bentuk, satu dianggap pertanda buruk dan yang lain pertanda baik sehingga perjalanan dilanjutkan.
long_description.en: An early text mentions a bird called Tigmamanuguin singing in a tree: on meeting it, or a serpent, a rat or someone who sneezed, people returned home at once, taking it as an augury of harm, especially when the bird sang. Its song had two forms, one taken as an evil omen and the other as a good omen, after which the journey went on.

long_description.id: Menurut kamus bahasa Tagalog tahun 1613 karya San Buenaventura, bila tigmamanukan terbang melintas ke kanan di awal perjalanan, perjalanan itu akan berhasil; bila ke kiri, para pengembara pasti tidak akan kembali, dan tanda itu disebut labay. Dikatakan pula bahwa pemburu yang menangkap tigmamanukan dalam jerat memotong paruhnya lalu melepaskannya sambil memohon agar burung itu berkicau di kanan.
long_description.en: According to San Buenaventura's 1613 Dictionary of the Tagalog Language, if a tigmamanukan flew across the path to the right at the start of a journey the expedition would succeed, and if it flew to the left the travelers would surely never return; the sign was called labay. It was also said that a hunter who trapped a tigmamanukan cut its beak and released it, asking it to sing on the right.

long_description.id: Dalam sedikitnya satu versi mitos penciptaan, Tigmamanukan membuka bambu tempat laki-laki pertama, Malakas, dan perempuan pertama, Maganda, keluar; dikatakan ia dinamai Manaul oleh Bathala, sedangkan sumber lain menyebut wujud burung Amihan yang mematuk bambu. Sebagian penjelajah Barat awal mengira burung ini burung biru peri (genus Irena), dan kebanyakan sumber sepakat bahwa ia berwarna biru; di Filipina kuno banyak burung pertanda lain juga berbulu biru.
long_description.en: In at least one telling of the creation myth, the Tigmamanukan opened the bamboo from which the first man, Malakas, and first woman, Maganda, emerged; it is said to have been named Manaul by Bathala, while other sources say it was Amihan's bird form that pecked the bamboo. Some early Western explorers took the bird to be a fairy bluebird (genus Irena), and most sources agree it was blue; many other omen birds of ancient Philippines were also blue-plumaged.

claims.quote: In Philippine mythology, the Tigmamanukan was believed by the Tagalog people to be an omen or augural bird. Although numerous other birds and lizards were observed for possible omens, particular attention was paid to the tigmamanukan. Before Christianisation, the Tagalogs believed the tigmamanukan was sent by the supreme deity and creator god Bathala

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Filipina, orang Tagalog meyakini tigmamanukan sebagai burung pertanda; di antara burung dan kadal lain yang diamati sebagai pertanda, perhatian khusus diberikan kepadanya, dan sebelum Kristenisasi ia diyakini diutus Bathala, dewa tertinggi dan pencipta.
statement.en: In Philippine mythology, the Tagalog believed the tigmamanukan was an omen or augural bird; among the other birds and lizards watched for omens, particular attention was paid to it, and before Christianisation it was believed sent by Bathala, the supreme deity and creator god.

claims.quote: The root of the word tigmamanukan is manók (from Proto-Austronesian *manuk), which in modern Filipino is exclusively used for the chicken (Gallus gallus domesticus).

statement.id: Akar kata tigmamanukan adalah manók (dari Proto-Austronesia *manuk), yang dalam bahasa Filipino modern hanya dipakai untuk ayam (Gallus gallus domesticus).
statement.en: The root of the word tigmamanukan is manók (from Proto-Austronesian *manuk), which in modern Filipino is used exclusively for the chicken (Gallus gallus domesticus).

claims.quote: According to San Buenaventura's 1613 Dictionary of the Tagalog Language ... the Tagalogs believed that the direction of a tigmamanukan flying across one's path at the beginning a journey indicated the undertaking's result. If it flew to the right, the expedition would be a success.

statement.id: Menurut Dictionary of the Tagalog Language karya San Buenaventura tahun 1613, orang Tagalog percaya arah terbang tigmamanukan yang melintas di awal perjalanan menandakan hasilnya; bila terbang ke kanan, perjalanan akan berhasil.
statement.en: According to San Buenaventura's 1613 Dictionary of the Tagalog Language, the Tagalogs believed that the direction of a tigmamanukan flying across one's path at the start of a journey indicated its result; if it flew to the right, the expedition would succeed.

claims.quote: some early western explorers say that the specific bird referred to by the name is a fairy bluebird (genus Irena and family Irenidae).

statement.id: Sebagian penjelajah Barat awal menyebut burung yang dimaksud nama ini adalah burung biru peri (genus Irena, famili Irenidae).
statement.en: Some early Western explorers say the bird referred to by the name is a fairy bluebird (genus Irena, family Irenidae).

claims.quote: It is said that the specific tigmamanukan that pecked the bamboo was named by Bathala as Manaul

statement.id: Dikatakan bahwa tigmamanukan tertentu yang mematuk bambu itu dinamai Manaul oleh Bathala.
statement.en: It is said that the particular tigmamanukan that pecked the bamboo was named Manaul by Bathala.

claims.quote: if they left their house and met on the way a serpent or rat, or a bird called Tigmamanuguin which was singing in the tree, or if they chanced upon anyone who sneezed, they returned at once to their house, considering the incident as an augury that some evil might befall them if they should continue their journey—especially when the above-mentioned bird sang.

statement.id: Menurut teks ini, bila di jalan mereka bertemu ular, tikus, atau burung bernama Tigmamanuguin yang berkicau di pohon, atau bertemu orang yang bersin, mereka segera pulang karena menganggapnya pertanda bahwa celaka dapat menimpa jika perjalanan dilanjutkan, terutama bila burung itu berkicau.
statement.en: According to this text, if on leaving home they met a serpent or rat, a bird called Tigmamanuguin singing in a tree, or someone who sneezed, they returned home at once, taking it as an augury that evil might befall them if they continued, especially when the bird sang.

claims.quote: especially when the above-mentioned bird sang. This song had two different forms: in the one case it was considered as an evil omen; in the other, as a good omen, and then they continued their journey.

statement.id: Menurut teks ini, kicau burung itu punya dua bentuk: yang satu dianggap pertanda buruk, yang lain pertanda baik, dan dalam hal kedua mereka melanjutkan perjalanan.
statement.en: According to this text, the bird's song had two forms: one was taken as an evil omen and the other as a good omen, in which case they continued their journey.

claims.quote: no one would go to heaven, where there dwelt only Bathala, "the maker of all things," who governed from above.

statement.id: Menurut teks ini, di surga hanya tinggal Bathala, "pencipta segala sesuatu", yang memerintah dari atas.
statement.en: According to this text, only Bathala, "the maker of all things," dwelt in heaven and governed from above.

claims.quote: The Tagalos adored a blue bird, as large as a thrush, and called it Bathala, which was among them a term of divinity.

statement.id: Menurut teks ini, orang Tagalos (ejaan teks itu) memuja seekor burung biru sebesar thrush dan menyebutnya Bathala, istilah ilahi di kalangan mereka.
statement.en: According to this text, the Tagalos (as the text spells the name) adored a blue bird as large as a thrush and called it Bathala, a term of divinity among them.

claims.quote: Tigmamanukin. A bird, also called tigmamanok, whose songs serve as an omen to the Tagalogs. Its scientific name is Jrena cyanogastra (according to Doctor A. B. Meyer).

statement.id: The Aswang Project mendaftar tigmamanukin, juga disebut tigmamanok, sebagai burung yang kicauannya menjadi pertanda bagi orang Tagalog; nama ilmiahnya ditulis Jrena cyanogastra (menurut Doctor A. B. Meyer).
statement.en: The Aswang Project lists tigmamanukin, also called tigmamanok, as a bird whose songs serve as an omen to the Tagalogs, giving its scientific name as Jrena cyanogastra (according to Doctor A. B. Meyer).

claims.quote: Limokon or Limukun. It is the Bagobo and Mandaya (Mindanao) name of the wild dove Phabotreron brevirostris whose song serves as an omen.

statement.id: Limokon atau Limukun adalah nama dalam bahasa Bagobo dan Mandaya (Mindanao) untuk merpati liar Phabotreron brevirostris yang kicauannya menjadi pertanda.
statement.en: Limokon or Limukun is the Bagobo and Mandaya (Mindanao) name of the wild dove Phabotreron brevirostris, whose song serves as an omen.

claims.quote: Before Christianisation, the Tagalogs believed the tigmamanukan was sent by the supreme deity and creator god Bathala as an oracle to mankind concerning whether or not they should proceed on a journey.

statement.id: Sebelum Kristenisasi, orang Tagalog percaya tigmamanukan diutus Bathala, dewa tertinggi dan pencipta, sebagai orakel bagi manusia tentang perlu tidaknya melanjutkan perjalanan.
statement.en: Before Christianisation, the Tagalogs believed the tigmamanukan was sent by Bathala, the supreme deity and creator god, as an oracle to mankind about whether or not to proceed on a journey.

claims.quote: In some Philippine creation myths, the tigmamanukan bird was sent by Bathala to split open the primordial bamboo whence the first man and woman came out.

statement.id: Dalam beberapa mitos penciptaan Filipina, burung tigmamanukan diutus Bathala untuk membelah bambu purba tempat laki-laki dan perempuan pertama keluar.
statement.en: In some Philippine creation myths, the tigmamanukan bird was sent by Bathala to split open the primordial bamboo from which the first man and woman came out.

claims.quote: Before Christianisation, as documented by Spanish accounts early in the colonial period, the word tigmamanukan was widely used for "any bird, lizard or snake that crossed one's path as an omen". Such encounters were called salúbong ("meeting", "encounter").

statement.id: Sebelum Kristenisasi, menurut catatan Spanyol awal masa kolonial, kata tigmamanukan banyak dipakai untuk "setiap burung, kadal, atau ular yang melintas di jalan seseorang sebagai pertanda"; pertemuan semacam itu disebut salúbong ("pertemuan").
statement.en: Before Christianisation, as documented by Spanish accounts early in the colonial period, the word tigmamanukan was widely used for "any bird, lizard or snake that crossed one's path as an omen"; such encounters were called salúbong ("meeting", "encounter").

claims.quote: The term most likely evolved from divination practises, i.e., reading omens following the ritual sacrifice of chickens and sometimes other animals like pigs.

statement.id: Istilah ini kemungkinan besar berkembang dari praktik ramalan, yaitu membaca pertanda setelah pengorbanan ritual ayam dan kadang hewan lain seperti babi.
statement.en: The term most likely evolved from divination practices, that is, reading omens after the ritual sacrifice of chickens and sometimes other animals such as pigs.

claims.quote: This sign was called "labay", a term still present in some Filipino languages with the meaning "proceed". If the bird flew to the left, the travelers would surely never return.

statement.id: Tanda itu disebut "labay", istilah yang masih ada di beberapa bahasa Filipina dengan arti "melanjutkan". Bila burung terbang ke kiri, para pengembara pasti tidak akan kembali.
statement.en: The sign was called "labay", a term still present in some Filipino languages meaning "proceed". If the bird flew to the left, the travelers would surely never return.

claims.quote: In any case, most of the sources which describe the tigmamanukan agree that it is distinguished by a "blue" color.

statement.id: Kebanyakan sumber yang menggambarkan tigmamanukan sepakat bahwa burung ini dicirikan oleh warna "biru".
statement.en: Most of the sources that describe the tigmamanukan agree that it is distinguished by a "blue" color.

claims.quote: In at least one telling of the Filipino creation myth, the Tigmamanukan was responsible for opening the bamboo from which emerged the first man, Malakas, and first woman, Maganda.

statement.id: Dalam sedikitnya satu versi mitos penciptaan Filipina, Tigmamanukan bertugas membuka bambu tempat keluar laki-laki pertama, Malakas, dan perempuan pertama, Maganda.
statement.en: In at least one telling of the Filipino creation myth, the Tigmamanukan was responsible for opening the bamboo from which the first man, Malakas, and first woman, Maganda, emerged.

claims.quote: however, in other sources, it was the bird form of Amihan, the deity of peace and wind, that pecked the bamboo. Some sources also state that Amihan's bird form is Manaul.

statement.id: Namun dalam sumber lain, yang mematuk bambu adalah wujud burung Amihan, dewi kedamaian dan angin; sebagian sumber juga menyebut wujud burung Amihan adalah Manaul.
statement.en: However, in other sources it was the bird form of Amihan, the deity of peace and wind, that pecked the bamboo; some sources also state that Amihan's bird form is Manaul.

claims.quote: It was also said that if a hunter caught a tigmamanukan in a trap, they would cut its beak and release it, saying "Kita ay iwawala, kung ako'y mey kakaunan, lalabay ka." ("You are free, so when I set forth, sing on the right.")

statement.id: Dikatakan pula bahwa bila pemburu menangkap tigmamanukan dalam jerat, ia memotong paruhnya lalu melepaskannya sambil berkata "Kita ay iwawala, kung ako'y mey kakaunan, lalabay ka" ("Kau bebas, maka saat aku berangkat, berkicaulah di sebelah kanan").
statement.en: It was also said that if a hunter caught a tigmamanukan in a trap, they would cut its beak and release it, saying "Kita ay iwawala, kung ako'y mey kakaunan, lalabay ka" ("You are free, so when I set forth, sing on the right").

claims.quote: Another kingfisher species was also called tigmamanukan. These birds were considered taboo to kill.
claims.locator: Other omen birds of the Philippine archipelago

statement.id: Satu jenis raja udang lain juga disebut tigmamanukan; burung-burung ini dianggap tabu untuk dibunuh.
statement.en: Another kingfisher species was also called tigmamanukan; these birds were considered taboo to kill.

claims.quote: The Tagálogs worshiped a blue bird as large as a turtle-dove, which they called tigmamanuquin, to which they attributed the name of Bathala, which, as above stated, was among them a name for divinity.

statement.id: Dalam kutipan sebuah catatan sejarah, orang Tagalog memuja burung biru sebesar tekukur yang mereka sebut tigmamanuquin, yang dinamai Bathala, nama bagi keilahian di kalangan mereka.
statement.en: In a quoted historical account, the Tagalogs worshiped a blue bird as large as a turtle-dove, which they called tigmamanuquin, to which they attributed the name of Bathala, a name for divinity among them.

claims.quote: There were myriads of species considered "omen birds" in ancient Philippines. Many of them share a characteristic: blue plumage.
claims.locator: Other omen birds of the Philippine archipelago

statement.id: Di Filipina kuno ada sangat banyak jenis burung yang dianggap burung pertanda, dan banyak di antaranya memiliki ciri yang sama, yaitu bulu biru.
statement.en: There were myriads of species considered omen birds in ancient Philippines, and many of them share a characteristic: blue plumage.
